$comment: 1. Must this invocation be passed straight through?
interactiveFlags OVERRIDES headlessFlags (agy -i looks headless, is not)
2. Can we CHOOSE the session id up front?   setIdFlag
3. How do we resume?                        resumeFlag / resumeSub
WHY setIdFlag MATTERS: when a vendor lets us pick the id, one identifier
names both the tether session and the agent's own conversation, so
restoring the terminal also restores the transcript. Without it, a
restored terminal comes back running a BRAND NEW EMPTY agent while
appearing to work. Only 4 of 12 vendors support it.
DO NOT ASSUME '-p' MEANS PRINT. It is --profile on codex, takes a value on
grok, and is --password inside `mimo run`. Every row is per-vendor for that
verified true  = `<bin> --help` was run on a real install and the flag read.
verified false = vendor docs only. Treat as a guess; confirm before trusting restore.

claude.notes: --session-id takes a UUID. Best-supported vendor here.

codex.notes: Top-level -p is --profile, NOT print: it must never trigger pass-through. Headless is the `exec` subcommand. Resume is a bare subcommand: `codex resume <id>`. Has no set-id flag (`codex --session-id x` errors with 'unexpected argument').

grok.notes: --session-id is LAUNCH ONLY. Its own help says it 'Does not resume existing sessions'. Using it on restore is exactly the silent-empty-conversation failure. Restore MUST use --resume.

agy.notes: Antigravity. Its hook key is conversationId, not session_id. --prompt-interactive/-i IS interactive despite the name, so it must override the headless flags. No set-id: confirmed absent from the flag listing AND the string does not appear in the binary.

gemini.notes: Docs only. Reported to exit fatally on a duplicate --session-id and on a missing --resume target, which is the good kind of failure.

pi.notes: --session-id creates if missing (idempotent), charset [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*, not UUID-only. Cannot combine with --session/--continue/--resume. -r/--resume takes NO value (picker). --session accepts a path or partial-id prefix; the transcript path is the identity.

opencode.notes: Server mints ses_<26 chars>; we cannot choose it. Prints 'Session not found' on a miss.

droid.notes: -r is mode-dependent (--resume interactively, --reasoning-effort under `droid exec`) so ALWAYS emit the long form. -s/--session-id CONTINUES rather than assigns. Behaviour on a missing session id is UNKNOWN - probe before trusting restore.

devin.notes: Behaviour on a missing session id is UNKNOWN - probe before trusting restore.

mimo.notes: Inside `mimo run`, -p is --password. Passes an unknown id through with no create-if-missing, so a bad restore is silent.

omp.notes: oh-my-pi (omp.sh), a fork of pi - NOT Oh My Posh. It dropped pi's --session-id; here --session is a plain alias of --resume.
